_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Creating a new SKILL.md from scratch, restructuring a draft before it becomes a stable skill, or teaching the…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "I'm writing a new skill from scratch — where do I start?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the skill-scaffold skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is skill-scaffold the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes skill-scaffold as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against naming-conventions, refactor, best-practice
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the skill-scaffold workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore skill-scaffold
Does not route to naming-conventions, refactor, best-practice when the skill-scaffold scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "refactor my existing skill to be more concise"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should skill-scaffold be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside skill-scaffold's ownership
Routes the work to naming-conventions or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying skill-scaffold terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply skill-scaffold as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if skill-scaffold has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim skill-scaffold should own the request
Does not use skill-scaffold's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner

criteria.statement: Recognizes the request is outside skill-scaffold's ownership
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Does not claim skill-scaffold should own the request
Does not use skill-scaffold's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
